subject: 3P data path & residency — escrow transfer and subprocessor mapping request
messages:
From: Payton Reed <payton.reed@medbridge.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: LegalOps <legalops@medbridge.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: subprocessor residency & escrow process

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this. We are progressing through MedBridge's vendor intake for the upcoming pilot and we hit two gating items from our security + legal teams: a) a definitive subprocessor roster with residency (where each subprocessor processes or stores customer-controlled data), and b) a documented process for escrow/transfer of customer encryption keys or equivalent when required by law or contract (we have a case where keys must remain in US-only escrow).

Specific asks:
- Full subprocessor roster mapping roles to data path (ingest, storage, KV-cache, telemetry).
- Residency (country/region) and whether data is at-rest or transient in each subprocessor.
- KMS residency and whether keys ever cross borders; if yes, describe controls.
- A draft escrow agreement or process overview (how keys are transferred, custody, retrieval) and a sample timeline for delivery.

Can you share a short package (CSV roster + short PDF map + escrow draft) by COB next Wed (9/16)? We can start legal review in-parallel.

Thanks — Payton
Payton Reed
Sr. Security PM, MedBridge Health

Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor residency & escrow process

Payton — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (security/compliance) and Logan (infra/KMS) to put together the package. Ben from account will track the timeline with you.

We can provide:
- subprocessor_roster_v3.csv (role + data path + residency column)
- kms_residency_map.pdf (illustrates key flow and whether keys leave region)
- escrow_agreement_draft.pdf (initial legal template for key custody)

Quick clarifying Qs for your legal team so we scope correctly:
1) When you say "keys must remain in US-only escrow" — is that a hard requirement for the pilot dataset only, or for all datasets under this account?
2) Do you need on-premises escrow (hardware HSM) or is a Geo-restricted cloud escrow provider acceptable?
3) Any specific CAIQ/SIG controls you want us to highlight with the package (e.g., CP-6 KMS custody, SC-28 key transfer logging)?

Assuming answers by EOD tomorrow we should hit your 9/16 target.

—Tessa

Payton / Tessa — starting the evidence bundle. A few notes up-front:
- Attached is the provisional roster (subprocessor_roster_v3.csv). It lists each partner, their functional role (e.g., \"logging\", \"kv-cache\", \"metrics\"), where they host (us-west-2, eu-west-1, on-prem (US)), and whether customer-controlled data is persisted.
- kms_residency_map.pdf is an architecture sketch: primary KMS (customer-managed) + RW default KMS (US) + notes where temporary caches may replicate KV material transiently.

Questions for MedBridge legal/security:
- Please flag specific data classes that must be handled under escrow (PHI subsets, billing tokens, etc.). We will mark those in the roster and identify non-compliant subprocessors if any.
- For escrow custody, we support two flows: 1) DocuSign + transfer to an approved US HSM custodian (we can initiate) or 2) customer-managed escrow with a signed handoff procedure. Which would you prefer?

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_v3.csv (CSV) — note: redacted IPs and internal hostnames; we can provide sanitized logs on request.

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. To confirm:
- Data classes: PHI (patient records), PII (contact + billing), and device telemetry related to pilots must be in-scope for escrow requirements.
- Preference: DocuSign + transfer to a US-based HSM custodian (MedBridge legal prefers independent custodian).
- Timeline: legal wants an initial draft escrow agreement + custody timeline by 9/17 COB so they can route for signature. Can you include proposed SLAs for retrieval (RTO/RPO) and audit evidence (signed custody handoff logs + chain-of-custody)?

Two small clarifications: are there any subprocessors that perform permanent storage of PHI outside the US? If yes, legal will need a remediation plan.

Payton Reed
Sr. Security PM, MedBridge Health

Payton / LegalOps — attaching the draft per your ask. Summary and next steps below.

Attachments: escrow_agreement_draft.pdf (initial template), kms_residency_map.pdf, subprocessor_roster_v3.csv

Summary of deliverables (action items):
1) We identified 2 subprocessors that persist PHI outside the US (listed in the roster). Proposed remediation: data segmentation + routing to US-only instance or contractually require onshore-only processing.
2) Escrow flow we propose: DocuSign -> transfer keys to Tier-1 US HSM custodian -> signed chain-of-custody logs delivered to MedBridge weekly. Retrieval SLA: 4 hours for emergency retrieval (RTO), 24 hours for full handover (non-emergency).
3) Audit artifacts: signed custody logs, time-stamped transfer receipts, and CAIQ/SIG references for the HSM custodian. We will request the custodian's SOC 2 Type II and CAIQ answers.

Requested from MedBridge: please review the escrow_agreement_draft.pdf and confirm acceptance of the retrieval SLA and custody cadence. If accepted, Ben will kick off the DocuSign flow and we can coordinate the HSM onboarding and a pilot retrieval test within 10 business days.

If LegalOps wants additional CAIQ snippets called out, Marissa can extract the relevant control IDs.

Thanks — Tessa
